title: Waluigi's Cut: The Roll Call at Trinity
subtitle: Eleven children, one clipboard, and an acronym that got explained by accident
pullQuote: She said, in a full classroom, that she is not on any list. Nobody contradicted her. Waluigi has filed that in two places so it cannot be lost.
standfirst: A new advisor took Classroom 2-B at Trinity General School, ran a roll call, and answered a question he could have let die in the noise. Waluigi was not in the room and has never been to Kivotos. Waluigi has opinions regardless.

sections.heading: The Man Came In Adjusting Glasses He Does Not Need
sections.body:
Waluigi wants to begin with the glasses, because the glasses are the whole man.

The record says he stepped through the sliding door adjusting a pair of spectacles that he does not require for vision. Not *needs and is vain about.* Not *forgot he was wearing.* The record is specific: he does not need them to see. He wears them anyway, and he touched them on the way in, which means he wanted the room to watch him touch them. Waluigi has been in this business a long time and Waluigi knows a costume when one walks past. The man arrived IN CHARACTER. He arrived, and he said **call me Sensei**, and he described himself as *the glue holding this whole operation together* — which is a strange thing to call yourself on day one of a job where you have met precisely nobody.

Then he spun around once and pointed at nothing in particular. WAH. That is not a criticism, understand. Waluigi has a great deal of professional sympathy for a man who spins and points, because Waluigi also has bits, and Waluigi also deploys them in rooms that have not yet decided whether to respect him. But it does tell you what he thought he was walking into, and what he thought he was walking into was an audience.

What he actually walked into was a JURISDICTION.

They came at him in order, and the order is the whole seating chart. From the window seats, a hand straight up: *does this mean you'll be around to chat during break too?* — which is a child checking, in the first fifteen seconds, whether this adult is the kind who leaves at the bell. From the front row, a formal welcome and the Sisterhood Club's assistance offered before he had asked for anything. Waluigi notes that one girl had already assessed him as someone who would shortly need help.

And then the door opened a second time, because Misono Mika had not finished arriving. She came through roughly ten seconds before the rest of the class had processed that anything was happening, and she did not walk to a desk. She went straight for HIS desk, slammed both palms flat onto it hard enough to set the pencil holder rattling, and demanded to know whether arriving first made her his favourite student.

Waluigi would like to award a medal here. Not for the entrance — the entrance is standard — but for what came next, which is that she sat down in the desk directly opposite his and adopted what the record calls a princess-like posture. Back straight. Hands folded. Chin elevated. She annexed the front of the classroom in under twenty seconds and then sat in it like it had always been hers, and Waluigi has watched grown warlords take three campaigns to accomplish less.

Then she offered him tea she had not brought.

**I didn't bring tea. But I *thought* about bringing tea. …The thought counts.**

Waluigi is obliged to report that the thought does NOT count. Waluigi is also obliged to report that it worked, because he did not correct her, and nobody in that room has corrected her in what sounds like years — a newcomer asked whether this was really the right place and was told, cheerfully, that Mika-senpai does this with every new teacher and you will get used to it, *oh, probably never, actually.* That is an institution describing itself. Mika is WEATHER. You do not object to weather.

And the man, catching the whispering, delivered his first real line of the morning: something about how if they were comparing him to their last advisor who *mysteriously disappeared*, he assured them he is much harder to get rid of.

Waluigi stopped the tape there. Waluigi rewound it. Waluigi played it again.

Nobody laughed. Nobody asked. Eleven children heard a stranger make a joke about the disappearance of the adult who previously stood where he was standing, and not one of them treated it as new information. Waluigi is going to be filing that sentence for a long time. He tapped the desk twice with a knuckle and called roll.

Waluigi will put it plainly. Waluigi has covered intakes at two war colleges, one monastery and a guild of licensed arsonists, and NOT ONE of them opened with a missing-persons joke. Waluigi flags it. Waluigi moves on. Waluigi will be coming back to it.

sections.heading: Eleven Names, Eleven Completely Different Ways Of Having One
sections.body:
A roll call is the cheapest characterisation device in the business and Waluigi has never seen one work this hard.

He went down the clipboard with his finger, efficient, and the class answered, and every single answer was a different species of answer. Kurimura Airi: present, with a wave, enthusiastic. Easy. Next.

Shirasu Azusa: nothing. Silence, and then a tiny voice from the corner mumbling something inaudible, and the advisor said *I'll take that as a yes* and moved on. Waluigi wants the geography of that corner on the record, because the record gives it and the record is right to. Her desk is in the far corner, angled slightly away from the room, as far from every other desk as a desk can get while still being furniture in the same country. Her posture was immaculate. Her pen was aligned exactly parallel to the edge of her notebook. A breeze came through a cracked window and pushed a strand of hair across her face and SHE DID NOT MOVE TO FIX IT. Waluigi has interviewed assassins with less self-control than that fourteen-year-old.

Ibaragi Yoshimi: a sharp intake of breath. That is it. That is her ENTIRE response to her own name — an audible flinch from the middle row, knuckles white on the desk edge, shoulders trying to fold her into a smaller volume. She got out *I'm here.* Then her eyes swept the room to find out who had witnessed it, landed on the advisor looking directly at her, and she flinched again and looked away fast. Waluigi will be blunt: that is not shyness. Shyness does not audit the room afterwards. That is somebody who has learned that being noticed has a COST.

Iochi Mari: a polite nod. Filed.

**…Shaggy.**

Dead silence. Heads turning. The advisor scanning the room and sighing through his nose before announcing that they were either missing Shaggy or he was hiding behind that sleeping kid in the back row. And a hand came up slowly from behind a desk near the window where the man had been crouched — CROUCHED — attempting to become invisible during ROLL CALL. He stood up with his slouch fully deployed, green shirt off one shoulder, and produced *uh… yo. Present. Like, hi.* His voice cracked on *hi.*

Waluigi does not know what this person is doing in Kivotos. Waluigi does not know how he got there or who enrolled him or why a lanky snack enthusiast with a documented dog is registered at an academy on a different plane from everything Waluigi thought he knew about him. Waluigi is choosing, for now, to simply write it down, because the archive has learned the hard way that demanding explanations up front only produces bad ones.

Then the clipboard produced **Lord Verity**, and the advisor squinted at it, looked around for anyone matching that description, found the newcomer sitting right there, arched an eyebrow, said *huh, you're Lord Verity? …Alright then,* and made a confident checkmark.

He was wrong. The correction did not stay quiet.

A chair scraped. A boy stood up. Every head turned. And:

**YES I AM LORD VERITY. AND I SHALL BE YOUR MASTER FROM THIS DAY FORWARD — KNEEL BEFORE ME, MORTALS!**

Stunned silence. A cough. Mika giggling. Airi covering her mouth. And the advisor blinking twice and going back to his clipboard with **…Right. Next.** Waluigi could not have handled it better and Waluigi is a professional.

The rest came fast. Kenzaki Tsurugi did not raise her hand at all — arms crossed, boots up on the desk, hair over one eye, a low *keheh*, and **…What a pain.** Asagao Hanae raised trembling fingers and whispered that she was here, *p-please take care of me,* sleeve over her knuckles, eyes down. Asa Hanko had to prompt him twice before he found the line. And one more student sat near the back watching, not leaning toward anybody, which in that particular room made them the most conspicuous person present.

Eleven names. Four minutes. Waluigi has read war councils with less in them.

And Waluigi wants one structural observation on the record before the next section, because Waluigi suspects it will matter later: the advisor got a name WRONG, assigned it confidently to the wrong child, and only found out because the correct claimant stood up and shouted. He is working from a list he has never checked against faces. Waluigi does not think that is laziness. Waluigi thinks NOBODY briefed him either.

sections.heading: The Adult Shouted Twice And The Girl Asked Once
sections.body:
Here is where the morning got away from him, and Waluigi wants it understood that this section is not about chaos. It is about who holds POWER in a room that has no formal power in it at all.

First the chaos, for completeness. Airi got out of her seat mid-proceedings and walked the aisle to the back with a second chocolate, weaving between desks with what the record calls practiced ease — *practiced*, meaning she does this, meaning this is a route she has taken before — and sat down next to Shaggy. She warned him not to let Sensei see him eating candy during the speech. He unwrapped it, ate it, and slouched lower, as though horizontal displacement were a form of stealth. Then he leaned in at a volume the record specifically flags as NOT REMOTELY QUIET ENOUGH and asked why Lord Verity was acting weird again and whether today was a cosmic alignment. His leg was bouncing hard enough to vibrate the desk.

At the front, the advisor raised his clipboard like a shield and went to volume. **ALRIGHT! SEATS! NOW!**

Nothing. Chairs kept scraping. Mika had, at some point nobody observed, relocated from her chair to the top of her desk. Waluigi wishes to note that she did not do this to defy him; she did it because the desk was there.

So he tried specificity instead of volume — *I don't care who you are or what club you're in, you sit down, you pay attention, and you behave like students. Not… whatever this is* — and his eyes swept a room containing Lord Verity mid-pose, Shaggy half-swallowed by his own hoodie, Azusa staring at a wall, and Mika spinning on her chair for reasons that remain unestablished. From the back, Tsurugi watched with her eyes narrowed to razor slits and pulled out her phone under the desk, thumb hovering, visibly weighing whether this was worth recording. **…What a circus.**

Waluigi notes she did not press record. Waluigi notes she considered it. There is a person in that back row who is building a file, and Waluigi respects a colleague.

Then Lord Verity escalated, because of course he did, slamming both fists down hard enough to rattle every pencil within two feet: **THIS CLASS WILL COME TO ATTENTION OR FACE THE WRATH OF LORD VERITY HIMSELF!** Airi giggled. Mika kept spinning. The back row did not look up. His wrath achieved a total measured effect of ZERO.

And then Iochi Mari stood up.

She did not shout. Waluigi wants that in bold and Waluigi wants it underlined twice on a whiteboard. She walked to the front. She positioned herself slightly behind the advisor's desk — not at it, BEHIND it, which is a spatial decision so deft Waluigi had to sit down for a moment — gave a small nod to the students nearest her, a silent signal, and said, softly:

**If everyone could take their seats properly, that would be wonderful~**

The record: *cutting through the noise more effectively than any shouting ever could.* Chairs clicking into place one by one *like dominoes falling.*

Waluigi has covered coups. Waluigi has covered the Regal Diet on a bad afternoon. Waluigi has watched men with titles and swords and standing armies fail to do what that girl did with one sentence, a hair-tuck, and a nod to three people she knew would move first. She has NO authority in that classroom. What she has is that everybody likes her and nobody wants to be the one person visibly ignoring her, and that is not a lesser form of power, it is the ACTUAL form, and the adult in the room had just spent two attempts demonstrating the inferior one.

What finally folded Lord Verity was a last warning — sit down or be removed. His fist was still up. The words died. The hoodie-cape slid off one shoulder and pooled on the desk behind him *like a deflated balloon,* and he said, in the best line of the entire morning:

**…You can't kick ME out. I'm not even IN anything yet.**

Then *fine,* through his teeth, and he sat. And the man thanked him for his cooperation with sarcasm the record measures as barely thin enough to pass through a colander.

Waluigi's finding for this section, stated flatly: the adult held the TITLE and the girl held the ROOM. Waluigi has seen that gap close badly in other institutions and Waluigi would like it noted early, while it is still funny.

sections.heading: He Could Have Let The Question Die And He Did Not
sections.body:
Now the part that turns an introductions session into a filing, and Waluigi wants to give the man his due before taking it back off him.

Seated at last, he leaned on the desk and started describing what the class IS. Students of Trinity General School. Here to learn, grow, be prepared for whatever comes next. Standard. Then: **SCHALE operations, academy life, the whole package.**

And from the floor, four syllables that Waluigi believes the man did not plan for: *SCHALE operations?*

Watch what that question does to the room, because the room answers it before he does. Lord Verity's eyes snapped to attention — real attention, the theatrical version gone in an instant, the pose melting *like frost in sunlight,* fingers tightening on the desk edge. **Wait. You're saying this class — THIS class — is connected to SCHALE? As in… actual missions? Real-world operations?** His voice cracked on *real-world.* And for exactly one second the record catches what is underneath the emperor act: *something raw — something hungry. Something that sounds like a kid who's been waiting for exactly this his entire life.* He started to say *I thought we were just—*, stopped, swallowed, and put the mask back on. The record says it no longer fit properly. WAH. Waluigi did not expect to be moved by the boy demanding that mortals kneel, and yet.

In the corner, Azusa's eyes sharpened — the record's image is *a blade being drawn from a sheath so smooth you'd miss it if you blinked* — and the name landed in her chest heavy and cold, because she already knows what systems that sort people into categories do to the people they sort. Yoshimi went shoulders-to-ears: *what does that have to do with ANY of us?* Hanae whispered the word to herself and got out **I… I know what that is** before her courage ran out at the two-second mark.

And then Shaggy said the thing.

**Like… okay, real talk. I've been at Trinity for a while now and nobody EVER explained this stuff to me. I get that there's Knights, I get that there's the Resistance, I even get that there's some kinda war going on — but 'operations?' Like… combat operations? Because if you're telling me I gotta fight something, I need to know where the nearest exit is first.**

Waluigi would like every institution in this archive to read that paragraph twice. A STUDENT of several years' standing, in good standing, enrolled, attending, has never had the organising structure of his own education explained to him. He knows there are Knights the way you know there is weather. He knows there is a war ON. NOBODY SAT HIM DOWN. And the only reason it came out at all is that a confused newcomer asked a question the returning students were too socialised to ask.

To his enormous credit — Waluigi is being sincere and it is costing him — the man put the clipboard down with a deliberate click, turned to face the room fully, held up a hand to stop Lord Verity interrupting, and answered.

**SCHALE isn't some secret club or a video game. It stands for Strategic Counter Hazard Activation League Execution.**

Asked whether that sounded stupid, he said: **It does sound stupid. I'll give you that.** Waluigi nearly stood up and applauded. An adult, in front of children, conceding that his employer's name is nonsense. Then the recovery, and it is a good one: it is not an acronym people throw around for fun, it is the backbone of everything keeping the city breathing, it decides which Knights respond to hazards, how resources get allocated, WHO GETS SUPPORT WHEN THINGS GO SIDEWAYS.

Mari translated for everybody too embarrassed to ask, opening with the mercy line — *most people don't fully understand it until they're told directly* — and landing it in three sentences: the framework that keeps Kivotos stable, coordinating Knight response and Resistance intelligence, turning strategy into missions. *The difference between knowing there's a threat and actually doing something about it.*

Waluigi notes the mercy line especially. She did not say *you should know this.* She said MOST PEOPLE do not, which hands every embarrassed child in the room a way to keep their dignity while learning something. Waluigi has watched professional diplomats fumble that exact manoeuvre.

Then the whiteboard, and the geography: Sectors 7 through 12, eastern perimeter, warehouses, supply routes, abandoned industrial buildings that make excellent hiding places for people who do not wish to be found.

sections.heading: One Sentence, No Evidence, Eleven Children
sections.body:
He wrote **THE RESISTANCE** on the board in block capitals and underlined it twice, and then he said this:

**They're criminals who want to tear down everything Kivotos stands for — the academies, the peace agreements, all of it.**

Waluigi is going to slow all the way down, because this is the paragraph where an archivist either earns his keep or admits he is a fan.

That sentence is not a finding. It is a characterisation of an armed political faction, delivered in one line, without evidence, to a room of fourteen-year-olds, by a salaried employee of the body those people are fighting. Waluigi is not saying it is false. Waluigi genuinely does not know, and Waluigi wants to stress that he has no romantic attachment to insurgencies — he has covered enough of them to know how many are exactly what the state says they are. It may be true. It may be precisely and completely true.

What Waluigi knows is that NOT ONE PERSON IN THAT CLASSROOM HAD THE INFORMATION TO TEST IT. That is the FINDING. Eleven students, one of whom had just admitted nobody had ever explained the basic structure of their own institution to him, received the moral status of the enemy as a single declarative sentence and had no means whatsoever of checking it. They could not have pushed back if they wanted to. They did not have the facts. Nobody has ever given them the facts.

So the archive files it where it belongs: as the advisor's CHARACTERISATION, attributed to him, dated, in his words. Not as a fact about the Resistance. Waluigi has written *ask again in twenty sessions* into the event record and Waluigi means it as a standing instruction to himself.

And then he turned around and looked directly at the student who had asked, and gave the short version: **we're going there because someone's been moving weapons through those sectors, and SCHALE is the group that stops that from happening. You — all of you — are part of that.**

*You are part of that.* Waluigi wants to note the grammar. Not *you will be asked.* Not *you may volunteer.* You ARE. Past tense of a decision nobody in the room remembers making. Eleven children found out in the same sentence that they belong to an operational structure and that the operational structure has already assigned them a side.

Waluigi has a professional weakness for institutions that say the quiet part out loud, because they are so much easier to write about than the ones that do not. This one said it on a Tuesday morning before the deployment rotation had even been read out. Waluigi thanks him and files against him simultaneously, which is the job.

Two things sit underneath this that Waluigi refuses to let scroll past. The first is that the entire disclosure — the acronym, the function, the sectors, the enemy — happened because somebody confused asked an unembarrassed question. A more careful man lets that first *SCHALE operations?* die in the classroom noise. He genuinely could have. It would have cost him nothing and there was no one in that room positioned to press him. He answered instead, at length, and the archive got its first interior view of Kivotos as a direct consequence. Waluigi, grudgingly, on the record: that is better than the average.

The second is that the answering is exactly what produced the damage. He was honest about the acronym, honest that it sounds stupid, honest about the sectors, honest about the weapons intelligence — and in the same honest breath handed a room of minors a one-line verdict on a political movement, with the full authority of an adult at a whiteboard behind it. Waluigi has seen a great deal of lying in his career. Waluigi is increasingly convinced that candour without context does more work for an institution than lying ever did, because the children will remember that he told them the truth about everything else. That is the trap, and Waluigi does not think the man set it deliberately. Waluigi thinks he walked into it holding a marker.

sections.heading: A Diplomatic Programme, Discovered By Being Seen
sections.body:
Two more questions landed before the briefing could resume and both of them opened something the man would rather have kept shut.

The first arrived almost casually: what about the pony liaison from Equestria, some were seen walking around the school, was that meant to be private?

Waluigi enjoys this question enormously, and not only because the archive has a registered Equestrian lunar calendar sitting in its data files, quietly indexed to Canterlot and Ponyville, waiting since before anybody here needed it. Waluigi enjoys it because of what the man's FACE did. The record catches it: expression shifting, just barely, just enough for anyone paying attention. Jaw tightening a fraction. Clipboard set down with a deliberate click — the same click he used before answering the SCHALE question, which Waluigi now believes is his tell for *I am about to say something I will have to justify later.* And then words chosen like a man stepping over a tripwire he cannot see.

**That's… a separate matter.**

It was not a denial, and Waluigi wants credit given where it is due: he could have made it one. Instead he confirmed the thing. A diplomatic initiative between Kivotos and Canterlot. Small groups, cultural exchange, goodwill built in advance of the kind of mess that requires actual military coordination. *It was supposed to be handled quietly.*

Then the exhale through the nose, and the admission:

**So the fact that you saw them walking around openly tells me someone dropped the ball on security protocols somewhere along the line.**

Read that again with Waluigi. The failure he identifies is not that the programme is secret from the students. The failure is that the students SAW it. The problem is VISIBILITY. He then instructed the room to report further sightings *to me — not to social media, not to your friends, to me. Directly,* which converts eleven children into an informal counter-surveillance net against their own school's guests roughly ninety seconds after he told them they were part of SCHALE. Waluigi is not even angry. Waluigi is taking notes, because that was fast.

And in the corner, a pen stopped.

Azusa had two pieces that would not fit: an organisation that runs on need-to-know, and diplomatic personnel strolling a school corridor in plain view. She wrote something brief IN THE MARGIN that was NOT part of the lecture. She said **…Understood** to nobody in particular. She straightened a page that was already perfectly aligned, and resumed. Waluigi would pay money to read that margin. Waluigi suspects the archive will eventually have to.

Airi, meanwhile, had four questions and no filter: are there snacks in Sector 7, are the ponies friendly, can she hug one, and do they get breaks. Waluigi refuses to treat this as comic relief, because *do we get breaks* is a labour question and the child asked it inside a deployment briefing.

Then Shaggy made the structurally correct observation that nobody else made — if we're dealing with bad guys AND ponies showing up uninvited, that's two different problems, right? It IS two different problems. The advisor said so: the Resistance is an internal threat operating out of Kivotos, the liaisons are an external diplomatic situation *that someone mishandled,* his tone carrying an edge that suggested he has a name in mind and is not saying it. **The fact that those two things intersected at this school without proper coordination is exactly why SCHALE exists.**

Waluigi notes, because it is Waluigi's actual job to notice this, that the man twice attributed the failure to an unnamed *someone* who dropped a ball, and that the disappeared previous advisor of this same classroom also remains an unnamed someone. Two unexplained gaps at one school inside one hour, both routed into the passive voice.

On the hugging, he was unambiguous: they are not your friends, they are diplomatic personnel operating under an agreement *that does NOT include hugging.* Correct, joyless, and — Waluigi admits — the funniest sentence any adult produced all morning.

Waluigi is keeping a column for unnamed someones now. It has TWO entries and the morning was not yet over.

sections.heading: He Explained Need-To-Know Ninety Seconds After Breaking It
sections.body:
**We can all use guns at least right?**

Waluigi has read the transcript of the two seconds that followed this question several times and Waluigi maintains that they are the most interesting two seconds in the filing, because of who filled them.

Not the advisor. Kenzaki Tsurugi. The girl with her boots on the furniture, who had contributed one *keheh*, one *what a pain*, one *what a circus*, and nothing else all morning. She did not look at whoever asked. She kept her eyes on the adult. She uncrossed her arms slowly and deliberately, leaned forward, and pointed at him like a blade:

**…Seriously? If you're about to say 'yes' to that, then this class is just an excuse for a shooting range and I'm filing paperwork.**

And then: **I've handled weapons since before most of you were old enough to stop putting them in your mouths.** Arms recrossing with finality. **Sensei. What's the actual plan?**

Waluigi wishes to be extremely clear about what just happened, because the surface reading is *scary girl is scary* and the surface reading is WRONG. The most responsible position taken by any person in that classroom — adult included — was taken by the delinquent in the back row with her feet up, and she took it AGAINST her own evident interest. She is the one person present with weapons experience. A yes to that question would have made her the most important student in the room. She argued against it anyway, on the grounds that a class which arms children is not a class, and her threat was not violence, it was PAPERWORK. She threatened to FILE. Waluigi has never been prouder of anyone in this archive.

Shaggy got himself on the record immediately and defensively — wanted it noted that he said nothing about wanting guns, described himself and Scooby as diplomatic solution kind of guys, offered a bag of Scooby Snacks as his contribution to the mission. Waluigi accepts the contribution and has logged it.

The advisor exhaled slowly and delivered it flat: **Nobody is handing out guns.** Stone-cold finality. One second of silence. Correct answer, correctly given.

And then he ruined it.

He held up a finger to preempt an objection that Tsurugi had not made and showed no sign of making — she had just finished arguing HIS side — and added:

**—except Tsurugi. You already have clearance.** A beat. **Everyone else: no.**

Waluigi put the tape down and went for a walk.

She did not volunteer that. It is nowhere in the record that she offered it, hinted at it, or asked him to confirm it. He disclosed a student's weapons clearance to ten of her classmates, unprompted, in order to add emphasis to an argument he had already won by a mile. Everyone in that room now knows which one of them is armed. That is not a small fact to hand eleven teenagers about one of their own, and it is a fact she alone should have controlled the release of.

Then — THEN — he turned to the whiteboard and wrote **need-to-know** in block letters and underlined it twice, and explained that SCHALE tells you what you need for your assignment and you do not ask about things outside it. Anyone whose role requires a firearm will be briefed separately, with proper safety training, by certified personnel. *Not me. Not YouTube.*

Ninety seconds. Ninety seconds between broadcasting a thing nobody needed to know and underlining the principle that you are not told things you do not need to know. WAH. Waluigi could not have constructed a cleaner demonstration if he had been given a year and a budget.

The record does not show her reacting. No *keheh.* No *what a pain.* Nothing. Waluigi finds that the single most informative non-reaction of the morning, and Waluigi has written it into the event file in two separate places specifically so that it cannot be lost in the noise of the outfit committee that formed four minutes later.

Waluigi wants one more thing understood about her. She asked *what's the actual plan* and she never got one. The girl who argued against arming children, who threatened PAPERWORK rather than violence, who had the only relevant experience in the room — she asked the single most practical question of the session and the session moved on. Waluigi has now counted THREE unanswered questions and Waluigi is only writing down the ones that were said out loud.

sections.heading: Nobody Answered Her, And Then Nobody Answered Her Either
sections.body:
What this class did with a war briefing is form a committee about clothes, and Waluigi refuses to sneer at that, for reasons that will take a few hundred words to arrive at.

It started because he said there would be no cool gadgets and no matching outfits — *at least… not yet* — and let it hang. Amateur error. Airi nearly took out a juice box getting up: **WE'RE GETTING OUTFITS?!** What colour, what style, matching or pick-your-own, could hers have chocolate mint on it somehow. From the back, Tsurugi's mouth twitched: *…Not yet, huh. How long do we have to wait? …Days? Weeks?* Waluigi notes that the girl who wanted no guns wants the outfit and wants a DATE for it. Yoshimi's eye twitched and she announced she was opting out of group matching, last time the school made her wear anything she looked like a kid playing dress-up, and then exhaled through her nose like a frustrated bull at Airi's bouncing.

He tried to reclaim it. The outfits line was a joke. *Mostly.* SCHALE is not glamorous, it is paperwork and logistics and getting the right people to the right places when things go wrong. **But it IS important. The Resistance runs through this system. Every Knight deployment, every supply line, every evacuation order during a hazard event — it all flows through SCHALE.**

And from the corner, flat, like a weather report: **Cute outfits. …Who cares about outfits.** A shrug barely worth the name. And then the question this entire filing is built around:

**The question is whether SCHALE actually works. Or if it's just another thing that sounds important but doesn't do anything for people who are already at the bottom of every list.**

Then her gaze dropped to a closed notebook with a pen aligned parallel to its edge:

**…Doesn't matter though. I'm not on any list. Supplementary students don't count for much either way.**

NOBODY ANSWERED HER. Waluigi has checked the record four times. The lecture simply continued.

The committee formed anyway, around the newcomer's declared preference for cute clothes, and Waluigi is now going to defend it. Lord Verity rose to bless the arrangement, pivoted mid-sentence into *an alliance that shakes the very FOUNDATIONS of… SCHALE training readiness,* pointed at the advisor, retracted, pointed lower, and settled for nodding sagely. Yoshimi called it what it was — *they're forming an ALLIANCE over a cape* — declared she was not joining any alliance, and then in the very next breath said *but if Sensei needs someone who actually reads the handouts…* and slapped a crumpled pamphlet on the desk: **I finished page six.** She had been waiting the entire session for a reason to say that. Waluigi felt it in his chest.

Hanae raised her hand like she was asking permission at a town hall, offered logistics and scheduling, then produced a notebook of neat handwriting and colour-coded tabs: she had already organised the SCHALE information, *there were gaps in the documentation so I cross-referenced it with the school's emergency protocols.* NOBODY ASKED HER TO. It had been hours. She found GAPS. Waluigi would hire her tomorrow. Told *what no eww* in response to her paperwork offer, she should have folded — and instead lit up *like someone just turned on a lamp inside her chest cavity* and volunteered to check uniform modifications against school regulations.
